column3: Night outside a small thatched hut in a seaside asura village, a small campfire drawn as flat crimson and rose shapes. The mother (Maa, from the reference) kneels beside her 12-year-old son (Tamra, from the reference), gently guiding his outstretched index finger; a glowing pale copper line of light hangs in the air where he drew it, lighting both their delighted faces. Stars, palm trees, the sea glinting behind. Tender, warm, magical.

The same village at night now in flames: huts burning, smoke soldiers (from the reference) with spears and torches storming in, villagers fleeing in silhouette. In the foreground Maa pulls the terrified boy Tamra behind her, shielding him with her arm, both looking back in panic. Chaos, flat crimson fire shapes, flying embers, dynamic diagonal composition.

The towering Smoke King (from the reference) rises out of a wall of black smoke in the burning village, his ember eyes glowing, one hand raised; coils of black smoke wrap around Maa like chains, lifting her off the ground as she reaches back toward her son. In the foreground the boy Tamra screams and reaches for her, held back by a smoke soldier gripping his shoulder. Terrifying, heartbreaking, low camera angle.

Seen from above: the boy Tamra falling backwards into a deep dark pit of ash and smoke, arms reaching up toward a small circle of red-lit sky; at the rim above, the huge silhouette of the Smoke King looks down. Ash flakes swirl around him. Vertigo, despair.

The bottom of a vast cavern of grey ash and broken rock. The bruised boy Tamra sits up, looking up through drifting ash toward a far-off mountain peak where a dark Indian palace stands, and at its highest tower a small cage glows with soft pale silver-teal light. A thin beam of moonlight falls on him. Lonely but hopeful.

The boy Tamra climbs a ledge of an ash cliff at dusk and looks up: streams of glowing pale silver-teal light, like rivers, flow across the dark violet sky from distant burning villages toward a far smoke-wrapped Indian palace on a mountain. Awe and urgency.

Inside a smoky ash cave, a young frightened smoke soldier (same armor as the reference but his fanged brass mask has fallen off, revealing a scared teenage face with ash-grey skin) sits on the ground with his spear knocked away, palms raised, begging. The boy Tamra stands over him holding his copper-banded staff, hesitating. Tension and mercy.

At the rim of the ash pits at dawn, the boy Tamra stands on a rocky edge; the copper tattoos on his forearms glow softly as if someone calls to him; ahead lies a vast misty marsh with drowned temple spires under fading stars. Hopeful, emotional.

The boy Tamra wades knee-deep into a still, mirror-like black marsh at night with jade-green mist and drowned Indian temple spires; his eyes glow faint cyan as he sees through illusions, while his reflection in the water looks slightly different and sinister. Mysterious.

Close-up looking down at the still marsh water: the boy Tamra kneels at the edge, and the reflection in the water shows his mother's face (Maa) half-transforming into the cruel smoke-wreathed face of the Smoke King, his ember eyes glowing. Tamra recoils in shock. Eerie, jade and violet light.

A gigantic face of the Smoke King formed out of black and ember-lit smoke looms over the night marsh, filling the sky, glaring down; tiny below on a stone, the boy Tamra stands defiant with his staff, his sash whipping in the wind. Epic scale contrast.

The boy Tamra steps out of the misty marsh and looks up at the colossal walls of an ancient Indian fortress-palace (Rajput style, black stone with gold trim, onion domes, chhatris), rising into a stormy violet sky full of black smoke and ember-lit windows. He looks tiny. Awe and dread.

Split vertical composition: at the top of a tall dark Indian palace tower, Maa inside a glowing cage made of smoke raises her glowing hand and sends down a beam of pale silver-teal light; far below on the battlements, the boy Tamra looks up and sees it, his face lit with hope. Night, lightning.

On the palace battlements at night: smoke soldiers and hooded archers raise the alarm, one strikes a huge bronze gong, archers draw smoking arrows, torches blaze; the boy Tamra sprints along the top of the wall toward the viewer with his staff, embers flying. Action, motion blur.

Looking straight up a dark Indian palace tower: a spiral staircase made of swirling black smoke winds up into the sky toward a glowing pale glowing cage at the top; the boy Tamra, exhausted and bruised, stands at the bottom step, looking up, panting. Vertigo, resolve.

The top of the Tower of Smoke under a storm sky: the Smoke King stands before a giant roaring ember fire, behind him Maa's cage of smoke with her pale silver-teal light being drained into the fire in streams; facing him, the small boy Tamra stands firm with his staff raised, the copper tattoos on his arms blazing. Climactic final confrontation, cinematic.
